channel.title: AI Frontier Post
channel.description: Dispatches from the AI frontier: AI news, research explainers, frontier lab coverage, and product comparisons.

item.title: Claude Fable 5.2 maxed its usage to make a 55-second motion-graphics film — and Reddit calls it scary decent
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: A Reddit creator gave Claude Fable 5.2 a premise and a day. Four concepts and 13 review rounds later, a 55-second motion-graphics film came back — written entirely as code. The thread’s verdict: “scary decent.”

item.title: Google DeepMind launches AlphaGenome 2: DNA predictions tuned to individual cell types
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Google DeepMind's AlphaGenome 2 predicts how DNA variants act in specific cell types, not tissue averages — trained on more than 107 million cell profiles, it finds nearly twice as many causal variants as its predecessor.

item.title: TSMC approves up to $1 billion in stakes in Anthropic and OpenAI
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: TSMC's board approved up to $500 million in Anthropic shares and up to $500 million in OpenAI preferred stock — the world's biggest chipmaker is buying into the two labs that drive demand for its most advanced chips, and the line between supplier and shareholder just got thinner.

item.title: Microsoft's 'Lazarus' backdoor hides in fewer than 10 dormant neurons — and needs no retraining
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Microsoft researchers have shown that reprogramming fewer than 10 dormant neurons in a language model can turn an AI agent built on it into a sleeper backdoor — no retraining required, and the model still passes its safety evals. The trigger can be as ordinary as a date.

item.title: Rumor: NVIDIA reportedly cancels the 24GB RTX 5080 launch as GDDR7 memory costs soar
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: NVIDIA has reportedly told its board partners the 24GB RTX 5080 won't launch in January, killed by the price of 3GB GDDR7 chips — and the 16GB card it was supposed to replace will stay in production. NVIDIA hasn't confirmed any of it.

item.title: ChatGPT’s Advanced and Standard Voice modes end December 11 as OpenAI goes all-in on GPT-Live
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: OpenAI will retire ChatGPT’s Advanced and Standard Voice modes on December 11, 2026, moving every voice user to the full-duplex GPT-Live model. The users who still prefer the older voices are pushing back — and OpenAI has reversed a voice retirement before.

item.title: Anthropic prices its IPO at $70–$78 a share, targeting up to $1.4 trillion
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Anthropic opened its IPO roadshow on November 10 at $70–$78 a share, a deal that would raise up to $64.35 billion and value the Claude maker at about $1 trillion — or $1.4 trillion on a fully diluted basis. Seven chip and cloud giants are buying $26 billion of stock on the side.

item.title: Stop your coding agent writing 2019 JavaScript: hands-on with Chrome’s Modern Web Guidance
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Chrome’s Modern Web Guidance hit Hacker News’ front page on November 10 with a simple pitch: 250 expert-written guides that stop coding agents writing 2019-era JavaScript. Install it, search it, scan a legacy codebase with it, and rewrite a dark-mode toggle the modern way — every command verified.

item.title: Qwen4-Max preview is live: Alibaba opens its next flagship model to developers
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Alibaba has opened a preview of Qwen4-Max, the flagship of its next model family, aimed squarely at coding and long-running agent work. It is live across Alibaba's developer tools — but there are no benchmarks, no model card, and no open weights yet.

item.title: Control your smart home with Claude: hands-on with ha-mcp, the 87-tool Home Assistant MCP server
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Home Assistant's community MCP server ha-mcp jumped to #7 on GitHub trending with 6,603 stars. Install it, point Claude at the public demo server, ask about your home in plain language, and build your first automation — every step verified against the live server.

item.title: Apple's leaked Harbor app would turn your Mac into a private AI inference server
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Apple is reportedly building Harbor, a Mac app that turns one or more Apple silicon Macs into a private AI inference server — no cloud, no command line. It leaked, it is in private preview under Apple's Claris brand, and there is no launch date yet.

item.title: Grok’s “anyone with the link” default left 35,578 apps open to the internet
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Security firm Claroc found 35,578 apps built with Grok — including SpaceXSI’s own confidential sales material — open to anyone on the internet, no sign-in required. The addresses were listed in passive DNS, and the sharing default did the rest.

item.title: Semantic search in a single SQLite file: build a local document search engine with sqlite-vec
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Vector search usually means a server. sqlite-vec puts it in one SQLite file: this tutorial builds a local semantic search engine over your own documents — embeddings, KNN queries, hybrid keyword search, and quantization — with every number measured, no API key, and no server.

item.title: AI 2027 authors now forecast superhuman AI researchers in 2027 — five months ahead of schedule
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: The AI Futures Project's authors say METR's finding — that Anthropic is improving its models about twice as fast as its historical rate, mostly because AI is doing the research — has pulled their timelines sharply forward. All six now expect superhuman AI researchers in 2027, with a 35–65% chance that AI able to automate all white-collar work arrives before 2028.

item.title: A webcam ‘X-ray mirror’ built with Claude Fable 5.2 overlays your skull in real time — Reddit’s verdict: cool demo, not a medical tool
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: A video posted to r/ClaudeAI shows a webcam app that pins a skull, brain and facial muscles to your face in real time — built in one chat with Claude Fable 5.2 in about 48 minutes for roughly $13. The thread loves the demo, and the author himself says it is not a medical tool.

item.title: Zoom AI Launchpad gives AI startups up to $150,000 in free credits for voice and conversation apps
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Zoom opened AI Launchpad on November 10, 2026: a grant program giving AI-native startups up to $150,000 in Zoom AI Services credits — equity-free — to build voice agents, conversation intelligence and multilingual apps on one API stack instead of stitching together vendors.

item.title: Qlik Talend Studio AI Assistant enters public preview to build, document and debug data pipelines
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Qlik put an AI assistant inside Talend Studio on November 10, 2026. Built on Qlik Answers and governed through Qlik Talend Cloud, it drafts data jobs from plain-language descriptions, documents existing pipelines and explains run-log errors — free during the preview for Premium and Enterprise customers, with general availability targeted for Q1 2027.

item.title: Google AI Edge Gallery adds offline speech recognition and text-to-speech — no internet needed
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Google added on-device speech recognition and text-to-speech to AI Edge Gallery on November 10, 2026. ML Kit transcribes 100+ languages at 10x real-time on Android, while open-weight models bring the same offline voice to iOS, desktop and the web.

item.title: Magpie vs LiteLLM: pick the right gateway for your coding agents
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Magpie (33,828 stars) and LiteLLM (63,054 stars) both put one gateway between your coding agents and every model — but they solve different problems. We installed both, routed Claude Code through each, and compared setup, subscriptions, failover, and cost tracking.

item.title: Businesses in ChatGPT: OpenAI launches Business Hub and Business Agents in beta
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: OpenAI launched Businesses in ChatGPT in beta, giving companies a way to claim their profile inside the chatbot used by 1.2 billion people a week — and to answer customers directly through a free Business Agent.

item.title: Fleet Tau 3.8: AI world model trained on 10 million synthetic Earths cuts copper-grade error by 38%
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Fleet Space Technologies launched Tau 3.8, an AI world model for mineral systems trained on ten million synthetic geological worlds. At a copper-gold project in Chile it predicted grades with 38% less error than conventional estimates — and up to 67% less on the deepest holes.

item.title: Anthropic launches Claude Sheets, Whiteboards and Meetings — Claude moves into the office
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Anthropic launched Claude Sheets, Whiteboards and Meetings in beta on November 10, 2026, and made Claude Data generally available — spreadsheets, whiteboards and dashboards your team builds with Claude, plus an AI that joins your calls.

item.title: Agentic coding with Kimi K3.1 Pro: build your own repo-aware coding agent
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Moonshot’s Kimi K3.1 Pro scores 65.7% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 at $2 per million input tokens. This tutorial builds a repo-aware coding agent on its API in one Python file — three tools, a loop you own, and a bill you can read off every run.

item.title: Gemini Robotics 2.5 puts humanoids on the Mercedes-Benz line — Apollo packs parts at 96% success
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Google DeepMind's Gemini Robotics 2.5 is its most capable vision-language-action model yet: tested on 200+ tasks with 30–100% higher success rates, and already running Apptronik's Apollo 2 humanoids on live Mercedes-Benz production lines at 96% pick-and-pack success — plus a new open ASIMOV-Jailbreak benchmark for robot safety.

item.title: An AI 'Karen' job interview went viral — and Reddit quickly spotted the script
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: A scripted video of an AI 'Karen' conducting a job interview with a man balancing a sneaker on his head pulled 5,800 upvotes on r/ArtificialIntelligence overnight — and the top comments clocked it as staged within hours.
